welcome_lead: Meet the building blocks every program uses: variables, types and operations.
meta_desc: GCSE Computer Science adventure on programming foundations: variables, constants and data types.
final_note: You now know the core ingredients of every program you'll write.

concepts.def: A named store whose value can change.
A named store whose value never changes.
A whole number with no fractional part.
A number with a decimal point, e.g. 3.14.
A value that is True or False.

walkthroughs.body_html:
score = 0 is a variable — we expect it to change.

PI = 3.14159 is a constant — by convention written in uppercase to show it should never be reassigned.

• int: 42
  • float: 3.14
  • bool: True / False
  • string: "GCSE"

Choosing the right type saves memory and prevents bugs.
The = symbol means 'store the value on the right into the variable on the left'. After x = 5, x holds 5 until reassigned.
